patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — LinkedIn Sales Navigator and RocketReach share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Comparison thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose LinkedIn Sales Navigator only if your buying job matches “LinkedIn’s AI-powered B2B sales tool for network prospecting, Buyer Intent, and InMail — C” rather than RocketReach's shape. Choose RocketReach only if your buying job matches “B2B contact database for finding professional emails, phone numbers, and company insights ” rather than LinkedIn Sales Navigator's shape. Workflow advantage: LinkedIn Sales Navigator leans lead-management; RocketReach leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — LinkedIn Sales Navigator and RocketReach share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: LinkedIn Sales Navigator is LinkedIn’s AI-powered B2B sales tool for network prospecting, Buyer Intent, and InMail — Core from US$119.99/mo; Advanced Plus for CRM sync.; RocketReach is B2B contact database for finding professional emails, phone numbers, and company insights with prospecting automations..
- Workflow coverage skew: LinkedIn Sales Navigator-leaning lead-management vs RocketReach-leaning —.
- Researched limits: LinkedIn Sales Navigator — Not a B2B email/phone contact database — InMail is designed to work without contact info; RocketReach — Not a CRM pipeline/deal manager..

Limitations — LinkedIn Sales Navigator: Not a B2B email/phone contact database — InMail is designed to work without contact info; No bulk InMail; messages are individual with monthly InMail credits (50/mo stated on plans); RocketReach: Not a CRM pipeline/deal manager.; Essentials is email-only; mobile/direct phones require Pro+..

Poor-fit cases: LinkedIn Sales Navigator is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a B2B email/phone contact database — InMail is designed to work without contact info · RocketReach is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a CRM pipeline/deal manager. · Avoid LinkedIn Sales Navigator if you actually need RocketReach's motion (B2B contact database for finding professional emails, phone numbers, and company)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
